solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Make black dynasty appealing (8)

blocks.note: to char is to scorch black

annotation.surface: An instruction to paint a ruling dynasty black and make it attractive.
annotation.walkthrough: "Make black" reads like a paint job, but it is the verb for scorching.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe a person or thing that attracts and pleases.

entries.clue: Brought up lingerie edged with fleece, a help when dating? (6)

indicatorNotes.Brought up: in a down clue, bringing a word up reads it bottom to top
indicatorNotes.edged with: the other word forms a border on both sides, so it goes round the outside

blocks.note: to fleece someone is to con them

annotation.surface: Frilly underwear trimmed with fleece, offered as a tip for a romantic evening.
annotation.walkthrough: The dating is not romance but scientific dating of old organic remains; the question mark flags the pun.
annotation.definitionFit: Radiocarbon dating measures a decaying isotope of this element to age ancient remains, so it is literally a help when dating.

entries.clue: Provide weapons for Gulf, where things might be hairy? (6)

annotation.surface: Arming a Gulf state, where the situation might get hairy.
annotation.walkthrough: "Hairy" in the surface means dangerous; in the definition it is literal.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a part of the body where hair grows.

entries.clue: How one works on fair to get extra income (9)

blocks.note: modus operandi, the way one works
fair, as in pale in colour

annotation.surface: Someone working on a fairground stall to earn a bit on the side.
annotation.walkthrough: MO is short for modus operandi, one's method of working.
annotation.definitionFit: The verb means taking a second, often secret, job at night for extra money.

entries.clue: State board promoting north-east (5)

indicatorNotes.promoting north-east: in a down clue, promoting the letters NE moves them up to the top of the word

blocks.note: a board of experts; its last two letters are NE, the compass abbreviation for north-east

annotation.surface: A state committee promoting the north-east region.
annotation.walkthrough: Only NE moves: lifted from the end of the board word to its front, the rest stays in order.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a Himalayan country, a sovereign state.

entries.clue: Rich vein covering a day (6)

indicatorNotes.covering: a cover goes over something, so the vein wraps round the A

annotation.surface: A rich seam of ore uncovered in a single day.
annotation.walkthrough: "Covering" takes only the A; the day follows on after.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal slang: someone with plenty of money is rich.

entries.clue: Killer vehicle almost missing MOT (4)

indicatorNotes.almost: almost the whole word is not quite all of it, so the last letter goes
indicatorNotes.missing: the named letters are absent, so they are taken out

blocks.note: the letters MOT removed from the front

annotation.surface: A lethal car that has somehow skipped its MOT safety test.
annotation.walkthrough: An MOT is Britain's annual roadworthiness test for cars, which makes the surface convincing; here it is just three letters to remove.
annotation.definitionFit: A shortened name: this sea mammal is known as the killer whale.

entries.clue: Private feature of St Paul’s brief criticism (8)

indicatorNotes.brief: a brief word is cut short, so it loses its last letter

blocks.note: St Paul's Cathedral in London is famous for its dome
STICK, criticism, without its last letter

annotation.surface: A private detail of St Paul's Cathedral drawing short, sharp criticism.
annotation.walkthrough: To give someone stick is British slang for criticising them.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of home and family life, as opposed to public affairs.

entries.clue: Put on The Godfather? (3)

blocks.note: the title of a Mafia boss such as Vito Corleone

annotation.surface: Screening The Godfather.
annotation.walkthrough: "Put on" suggests staging the film; it means to dress in. The question mark marks the Godfather as one example of a Mafia boss.
annotation.definitionFit: One sense is to get dressed in a garment; the other is the Italian honorific given to a Mafia head.

entries.clue: Any real musical periodically dropped in song of praise (8)

indicatorNotes.periodically dropped: letters dropped at regular periods, so every other one goes

annotation.surface: Any genuine musical number has been cut from a hymn.
annotation.walkthrough: The odd-numbered letters of the two words are the ones thrown away.
annotation.definitionFit: A Hebrew-derived cry of praise to God, sung in hymns and liturgy.

entries.clue: Australian bouncer grabbing setter’s lover (5)

indicatorNotes.grabbing: to grab is to take hold of, so the outer word closes round the other

annotation.surface: A nightclub doorman in Australia getting hold of the puzzle-setter's boyfriend.
annotation.walkthrough: "Bouncer" is not a doorman but a kangaroo.
annotation.definitionFit: An eponym: Shakespeare's young hero gave his name to any ardent male lover.

entries.clue: Force member‘s awkward clam open when touring island (9)

indicatorNotes.awkward: awkward means clumsy, so the letters come out in an ungainly order
indicatorNotes.when touring: a tour goes round a place, so these letters go round the island

annotation.surface: A member of the armed forces awkwardly prising open a clam on an island tour.
annotation.walkthrough: "Force" is the police force, not the military.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a member of the police force.

entries.clue: Window that is left on order after vacation (5)

indicatorNotes.after vacation: a vacated room is emptied, so the word loses its middle and keeps its outer letters
indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, placed on means coming after

annotation.surface: A window left open on instructions after the holidays.
annotation.walkthrough: "Vacation" suggests a holiday, but here it means emptying out a word.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a projecting bay window on an upper floor.

entries.clue: Albanian money includes English national emblem (4)

indicatorNotes.includes: to include is to hold within, so the currency surrounds the E

annotation.surface: Albanian currency featuring an English national symbol.
annotation.walkthrough: The emblem wanted is Welsh, not English: "English" only supplies the E.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this vegetable is the national emblem of Wales.

entries.clue: University service ignoring defect in drug addict (4)

indicatorNotes.ignoring: what is ignored is left out, so those letters go

annotation.surface: A campus support service that overlooks a flaw in someone on drugs.
annotation.walkthrough: A vice is a moral defect, and it sits neatly at the end of the service word.
annotation.definitionFit: Slang: someone who takes drugs habitually.

entries.clue: Boil second half of drink (4)

indicatorNotes.second half of: of a word split in two, keep only the latter half

annotation.surface: Heating up the rest of a drink.
annotation.walkthrough: The drink must be found first, an eight-letter word for any drink; only its back four letters are used.
annotation.definitionFit: Figurative: to boil with anger is to be furious.

entries.clue: Late bloomer caught fruit bobbing across lake (4,8)

indicatorNotes.caught: as in catching what someone says: take the sound
indicatorNotes.across: stretched across something, so the word spans either side of it

blocks.note: the ugli fruit, a citrus hybrid

annotation.surface: Fruit bobbing about on a lake, just as a late-flowering plant is caught up.
annotation.walkthrough: "Caught" looks like cricket's C, but it means heard.
annotation.definitionFit: From Andersen's fairy tale: the scorned cygnet that grows into a swan, so anyone who blossoms late.

entries.clue: Unknown author not at first compliant (8)

indicatorNotes.not at first: the word is not there at its first position, so its first letter goes

blocks.note: algebra's unknowns are x, y and z
Henry FIELDING, author of Tom Jones, without his F

annotation.surface: An anonymous writer who wasn't cooperative at first.
annotation.walkthrough: "Not at first" reads as a timeline, but it strips the author's initial letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: giving way readily to pressure or requests.

entries.clue: Begin kid’s first tracksuit, wrongly having lost uniform (4-5)

indicatorNotes.first: the first of the word is its opening letter
indicatorNotes.wrongly: done wrongly, the letters are set out in the wrong order
indicatorNotes.having lost: what is lost is no longer there, so that letter goes

blocks.note: TRACKSUIT without U (uniform, NATO alphabet), rearranged

annotation.surface: A child starting out in a tracksuit, but wrongly without the school uniform.
annotation.walkthrough: Uniform is the NATO phonetic word for U.
annotation.definitionFit: Figurative, from starting a motorbike with a kick: to get something going.

entries.clue: Revered figure‘s form of cricket before noon (4)

blocks.note: One Day International, a cricket format

annotation.surface: A cricketing hero's style of play before lunch.
annotation.walkthrough: A one-day international is a limited-overs cricket match between national teams.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the chief god of Norse mythology.

entries.clue: Tunbridge Wells weirdly not having gel, but somehow he profits dishonestly (8)

indicatorNotes.weirdly: weird means strange, so the letters are jumbled
indicatorNotes.not having: without the named letters, so they are struck out
indicatorNotes.somehow: done somehow, in some unspecified way, so the leftovers are rearranged

blocks.note: letters of GEL and BUT removed

annotation.surface: A resident of Tunbridge Wells who shuns hair gel yet cheats for gain.
annotation.walkthrough: Tunbridge Wells is a genteel Kent town, a byword for respectable middle England, which makes a crook there a neat surprise.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: a cheat who takes money by fraud.

entries.clue: Miserable work on the house, eating what toast? (4,3,5)

indicatorNotes.eating: what is eaten goes inside, so the outer word swallows the other

blocks.note: to put a straw roof on a house

annotation.surface: Grim renovation work, then eating toast.
annotation.walkthrough: "Toast" suggests bread, but it is a drinking toast; the two-letter query goes in after the roofing word's second letter.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: said as a toast before knocking back a drink.

entries.clue: Pupil picked up skirt (6)

indicatorNotes.picked up: as a radio picks up a signal: what is heard

blocks.note: a pupil living at boarding school

annotation.surface: A schoolchild grabbing a skirt.
annotation.walkthrough: "Skirt" looks like a garment, but it is the verb: to skirt a field is to run along its edge.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to skirt something is to lie along its edge.

entries.clue: Medical centre welcomes queen, not popular minister (6)

indicatorNotes.welcomes: to welcome is to take in, so the clinic surrounds the queen
indicatorNotes.not: the popular word is not there, so its letters go

annotation.surface: A clinic receives the queen, but no popular government minister.
annotation.walkthrough: The minister is a church minister, not a government one.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a minister of religion, a member of the clergy.

entries.clue: About to abandon dog in square (4)

indicatorNotes.to abandon: what abandons a word leaves it, so those letters go

blocks.note: a member of the dog family

annotation.surface: Being told to abandon your dog in the town square.
annotation.walkthrough: "Square" means a square number, not a town square.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: three squared, a square number.

entries.clue: Unintroduced woman who raised Cain? (4)

indicatorNotes.Unintroduced: without its introduction, so the word loses its opening letter

annotation.surface: A woman who caused trouble, never formally introduced.
annotation.walkthrough: To raise Cain is to cause uproar; here it is literal.
annotation.definitionFit: In Genesis the first man fathered and raised Cain, so the idiom is read literally.

entries.clue: Prophet Hosea extremely bereft in written document (5)

indicatorNotes.extremely bereft: bereft of its extremes, so the first and last letters go
indicatorNotes.in: one thing in another sits inside it, so the letters go within the document

annotation.surface: The prophet Hosea left out of a written text.
annotation.walkthrough: Hosea looks like the definition, being a prophet himself; he is only wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Hebrew prophet who led the Israelites out of Egypt.

entries.clue: Damage earth around edge of park (5)

indicatorNotes.around: goes around, so the earth word surrounds the letter
indicatorNotes.edge of: the edge is the outermost point, here the start of the word

annotation.surface: Harm done to the soil around the edge of a park.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads straight as gardening damage, so the only trick is spotting that the earth goes round a single letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to ruin or harm something.

entries.clue: Grind cold cut (4)

blocks.note: to hew is to cut, as with an axe

annotation.surface: Grinding up a cold cut of meat.
annotation.walkthrough: "Cold cut" reads as sliced meat, but the phrase splits into two pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: working food between the teeth.

entries.clue: Hard veterans show affection (4,5)

annotation.surface: Tough old soldiers showing a soft side.
annotation.walkthrough: "Hard veterans" looks like one tough group, but hard supplies only its abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: clasping another's hand is a gesture of affection.

entries.clue: Carrion eaters no longer having desire for bears (3)

indicatorNotes.no longer having: the scavengers no longer have those letters, so they come out

annotation.surface: Scavengers that have lost their appetite for bears.
annotation.walkthrough: "Bears" looks like the animals, but it is the verb, as in bearing a scar.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to bear something is to carry or possess it.

entries.clue: Maybe how to form a comparative adjective for snake (5)

annotation.definition2: how to form a comparative adjective

blocks.clueFragment: how to form a comparative adjective
blocks.note: the instruction for turning big into bigger, read as two words

annotation.surface: A grammar lesson on the right comparative for a snake.
annotation.walkthrough: Read as an instruction, the answer splits into a verb and a suffix: fast becomes faster. "Maybe" admits not every comparative works this way.
annotation.definitionFit: One sense is the viper, Britain's only venomous snake; the other is the instruction to tack a suffix onto an adjective.

entries.clue: Stretch limo initially bends round (6)

indicatorNotes.initially: at its start, so only the word's opening letter
indicatorNotes.round: turned round, so the letters are read back to front

annotation.surface: A stretch limousine negotiating the bends.
annotation.walkthrough: "Stretch limo" is a single phrase in the surface; split it, and the first word is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to spread or extend out loosely.

entries.clue: Strangely secret, with each bit hidden? (8)

indicatorNotes.Strangely: arranged strangely, so the letters are in an odd order

blocks.note: a binary bit is 0 or 1, read as the letters O and I

annotation.surface: A strangely secret code with every bit concealed.
annotation.walkthrough: "Bit" is the computing term: each bit is a 0 or a 1, which pass as O and I.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: knowledge understood only by an inner circle is in effect hidden.
